record.title: Rigid Polyurethane Foams’ Development and Optimization from Polyols Based on Depolymerized Suberin and Tall Oil Fatty Acids
claim_notes: Original article asset retained and inspected on 2026-10-05; no formal version number verified.

Retained inspected original source SHA-256 4e0c1a91a9ae26d814576961a3805f9371b46498d4861fb578e7a413bb4c726d, 184537 bytes, corresponds to https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC11013755/fullTextXML. Independent source-transcription review confirmed the selected value and article-specific rights; this is not scientific replication.

License CC-BY-4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Article-specific notice verified for the original selected study facts; no selected third-party comparison is imported. Adaptations are selected factual transcription, structured metadata, authored multilingual labels and scope qualifications; source number and unit precision remain unchanged. PDFs, full tables, figures, XML/HTML, screenshots and source dumps are not bundled or relicensed under project MIT.

Only the optimized Lupranol-based LPO-1 rigid PUR formulation characterized in this study. Lupranol 3300/3422 polyether polyols and polymeric MDI distinguish this formulation; it is not the suberin-based SPO series despite the article title. LPO-1 is a study formulation, not a certified product grade. Do not count LPO-2/LPO-3 as extra identities or substitute modeled target/normalization densities.

historical_scope.exact_historical_source_scope: Only the optimized Lupranol-based LPO-1 rigid PUR formulation characterized in this study. Lupranol 3300/3422 polyether polyols and polymeric MDI distinguish this formulation; it is not the suberin-based SPO series despite the article title. LPO-1 is a study formulation, not a certified product grade. Do not count LPO-2/LPO-3 as extra identities or substitute modeled target/normalization densities.

exact_historical_identity_scopes.mat_ivdre2024_lpo1_rigid_pur: Only the optimized Lupranol-based LPO-1 rigid PUR formulation characterized in this study. Lupranol 3300/3422 polyether polyols and polymeric MDI distinguish this formulation; it is not the suberin-based SPO series despite the article title. LPO-1 is a study formulation, not a certified product grade. Do not count LPO-2/LPO-3 as extra identities or substitute modeled target/normalization densities.
exact_historical_identity_scopes.mat_ivdre2024_spo2_rigid_pur: Study-defined SPO-2 rigid polyurethane formulation based on synthesized suberinic-acid/tall-oil-derived polyols. The Table 9 inputs are 67 g SA-C_TOFA(50:50)/TMP and 33 g SA-E_ETOFA(50:50)/TMP, unlike the existing LPO-1 Lupranol 3300/3422 formulation. This is one selected representative of the SP formulation series, not all suberin-derived polyurethane foams. SPO-2 is a study label, not a certified grade. Do not count SPO-1/SPO-3, LPO-2/LPO-3, cure times, specimens or translations as extra identities in this packet. No final molecular formula, purity, elemental composition or universal material equivalence is inferred.

historical_scope.new_review_basis: The existing source and old identity/state/property objects remain unchanged. Their prior scope does not itself authorize any additional label. This separate review uses primary Table 9 evidence that LPO-2 changes principal Lupranol inputs from 40/60 to 66/34 g, and SPO-3 changes principal suberin/tall-oil polyol inputs from SPO-2 67/33 to 40/60 g. These explicit formulation changes support only the two selected additions; source labels or catalyst/blowing-agent changes alone do not.
historical_scope.omitted_formulations: LPO-3 and LPO-1 share a 40/60 principal-polyol ratio; SPO-1 and SPO-3 also share a 40/60 principal-polyol ratio. Their complete formulations differ, so this conservative exclusion does not assert chemical equivalence. The unselected SPO-1 density discrepancy is preserved.

exclusions: SPO-1: same principal 40/60 polyol ratio as selected SPO-3; full recipe differs, so no claim of chemical equivalence. Do not add identity credit from catalyst/blowing-agent changes alone. Its 43.9 kg/m3 density conflicts with the stated 40.7-43.5 range.
LPO-3: same principal 40/60 Lupranol ratio as existing LPO-1; full recipe differs, so exclusion is conservative identity policy, not asserted chemical equivalence.
